_meta.description: Quest dialogue for MQ-22: The Marshal Speaks. Year 2 Autumn — broadcast ultimatum + NPC reactions.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [A sharp burst of static erupts from every radio in Coppervale. Then a voice — calm, measured, terrifyingly composed.]

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: People of the Beacon Towns. My name is irrelevant. You know me as the Marshal. I address you now not as an enemy, but as a realist.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: For two years I have watched you cling to the ruins of the old world, scavenging like rats in a graveyard. Building your little walls. Playing at civilization.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: But civilization requires order. And order requires strength. You have neither. What you have is a borrowed clock — and I am here to tell you that time is up.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: When winter comes, I will take Coppervale. Not because I hate you. Because the world cannot afford your weakness. Surrender your technology, your AI, and your engineer — and I promise your people will be treated fairly under my protection.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: Resist, and I will demonstrate what real strength looks like. You have until the first snow. Choose wisely.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [The broadcast ends. Silence hangs over Coppervale like a held breath.]

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: Everyone... please. I know you're frightened. I am too. But panicking helps no one.

lines.speaker: npc_harrow
lines.text: He's given us a timeline. That's both a threat and a gift. We know when he's coming. That means we can prepare.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: I've already sent word to the Council. If our alliance holds, reinforcements can arrive before the snow. But we need to move fast.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: I have analyzed the broadcast signal. It originated from the Scorchlands — approximately 80 kilometers southeast. He has a permanent base of operations.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: And Jack... he asked for me specifically. He knows what I am. That means he knows what the AEGIS network was designed to do.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Then he's not just after territory. He wants control of the old military systems.

lines.speaker: npc_harrow
lines.text: Which means we don't just need to defend Coppervale. We need to make sure he never gets his hands on that technology. Ever.

lines.speaker: npc_spark
lines.text: He wants to take our workshop? OUR machines? Over my cold, dead, grease-stained hands. I'm tripling production on turret components starting NOW.

lines.speaker: npc_maren
lines.text: I've survived worse than a bully with a radio, dear. My Oren faced down raiders when this town was nothing but tents. We endured then. We'll endure now.

lines.speaker: npc_pip
lines.text: Mister Jack? Are the bad men really coming? I... I can help! I've been practicing with the scanner, just like you showed me!

lines.speaker: npc_elm
lines.text: In times like these, we must remember what we're fighting for. Not just walls and machines — but each other. I'll be in the chapel if anyone needs to talk.

lines.speaker: npc_leera
lines.text: A siege? Good. I've been itching for a real fight. Those patrol skirmishes barely count. Let them come — we'll show them what Coppervale steel can do.

lines.speaker: npc_michelle
lines.text: I need to prepare the clinic for mass casualties. Jack, can you help me stockpile medical supplies? Bandages, antiseptic, splints. We'll need everything.

lines.speaker: npc_kaydee
lines.text: Well. That's one way to ruin a perfectly good autumn. I'll start rationing the good whiskey — we'll need it after, not before.

lines.speaker: npc_kiery
lines.text: I... I thought we were safe here. I thought I'd found somewhere that wouldn't be taken from me again.

lines.speaker: npc_kiery
lines.text: But I'm not running. Not this time. Whatever you need, Jack. I'm here.

lines.speaker: npc_paige
lines.text: I'm going to document everything. Every preparation, every conversation, every moment of courage. This town's story deserves to be remembered, whatever happens.

lines.speaker: npc_gus
lines.text: I'm converting the back storage into an emergency shelter. Thick walls, supplies for two weeks. The children and elderly go there first if the walls are breached.

lines.speaker: npc_ferris
lines.text: I can modify the radio to jam their communications during the attack. It'll burn out the transmitter, but if it gives us even an hour of confusion...

lines.speaker: npc_hank
lines.text: I'll forge day and night if I have to. Every bolt, every plate, every blade. The smithy doesn't close until that man is beaten.

lines.speaker: npc_bramble
lines.text: I've seen siege injuries before, in my years traveling. Crush wounds, burns, shrapnel. I'll assist Michelle. Two medics are better than one.

lines.speaker: npc_nora
lines.text: I'll organize the food stores. Preservation, rationing, emergency cooking. If we're under siege, nobody goes hungry on my watch.

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: The town knows what's coming. And not a single person has asked to leave. Jack, I've never been prouder of this place.

lines.speaker: npc_harrow
lines.text: Pride won't stop arrows. But it'll keep people standing when the arrows fly. That's something.
